uncertainties: R2's proposed retention is self-justified compensation, not clearly restitution or trust repair.
Individual bucket choices and retrospective explanations in R2–R6 do not independently establish rule transitions.
R3's unequal exchanges do not clearly establish forgiveness of misconduct or a specified shortfall.
R7's more-than-half practice overlaps earlier five-bucket returns; it does not clearly replace the four-or-five custom.
R9's infinite trust and caution-free covenant may be idealized metaphor rather than a new decision rule; role reversal stages the demonstration.
R9's total sending does not contradict R3's restriction on returning all receipts.
The restoration omission in R8–R10 does not establish revocation, forgetting, or contradiction of R6.
R8 and R10 discuss intentions and trust depth without an explicit blame-versus-error contrast.
